points.quote: You should only use AI tools, including generative AI, to the extent that has been outlined in the assessment brief.
points.anchor: 3. AI and Academic Integrity and Misconduct
points.gist: Use AI tools only to the extent the assessment brief outlines.

points.quote: 3.6. Where the use of AI tools including generative AI is permitted you must: 3.6.1. Reference the use in your work (see section 4 below) 3.6.2. Briefly outline your AI use in the AI Declaration (see section 5 below) 3.6.3. Keep a record of the tools, prompts and outputs (see section 6 below).
points.anchor: 3. AI and Academic Integrity and Misconduct
points.gist: Where AI use is permitted, students must reference it, outline it in the AI Declaration, and keep a record of tools, prompts and outputs.

points.quote: The AI Declaration must be submitted with all assessments submitted to, or completed on, Moodle, including those where no AI use is permitted by the Assessment Brief.
points.gist: An AI Declaration must accompany all Moodle assessments, even where no AI use is permitted.

points.quote: you will have up to 24 hours after the submission to complete and submit the AI Declaration.
points.gist: Students have up to 24 hours after submission to complete and submit the AI Declaration.

points.quote: In-person assessments such as exams, in-class tests and purely practical assessments do not require an AI Declaration to be submitted.
points.gist: In-person exams, in-class tests and purely practical assessments do not require an AI Declaration.

points.quote: Provide a summary (up to 250 words) of how you used AI tools including generative AI in your work, in line with the assessment brief.
points.gist: Users of AI complete a summary of up to 250 words describing how AI was used.

points.quote: You do not have to submit evidence of prompts and outputs with the AI Declaration, however if your work is flagged for possible academic misconduct, you may be asked to provide evidence to show that your use was in line with the permitted parameters of the Assessment Brief.
points.gist: Evidence of prompts and outputs need not be submitted, but may be requested if work is flagged for possible misconduct.

points.quote: It is expected that references to AI outputs will include: (i) the name of the AI platform, (ii) the date of use, (iii) the person who input the prompt.
points.anchor: 4. Referencing the use of AI tools in your work
points.gist: References to AI outputs are expected to give the platform name, date of use and the person who entered the prompt.

points.quote: OpenAI ChatGPT (2024). ChatGPT response to YOUR NAME, 1 January 2024.
points.anchor: 4. Referencing the use of AI tools in your work
points.gist: A Harvard reference example: OpenAI ChatGPT (2024). ChatGPT response to YOUR NAME, 1 January 2024.

points.quote: Academic staff use the Turnitin originality (AI) checker which flags AI use in an assessment. They then check this against the permitted use outlined in the assessment brief as well as your statement in the AI Declaration.
points.gist: Staff use the Turnitin AI checker, then compare any flag with the assessment brief and the student's AI Declaration.

points.quote: Failure to submit a completed Declaration with your work may be taken into account during an investigation if your work is subsequently flagged for possible academic misconduct
points.gist: Not submitting a completed Declaration may be taken into account in an investigation if work is flagged.

points.quote: If the assessment brief does not explicitly mention the use of AI tools including generative AI, you should adhere to the Supporting Good Academic Practice Policy.
points.anchor: 3. AI and Academic Integrity and Misconduct
points.gist: If the brief does not mention AI, follow the Supporting Good Academic Practice Policy.

points.quote: If you complete this declaration and have not properly referenced AI in your work it will still be flagged for academic integrity.
points.anchor: Appendix 1: Copy of the AI Declaration
points.gist: Completing the declaration without properly referencing AI in the work will still lead to an academic integrity flag.

points.quote: There may be legitimate uses for AI, especially in the preparatory stages of your work, for example, in helping you summarise and analyse complex materials, extract key findings, break writer’s block and highlight grammatical errors.
points.anchor: 2. Guidance on when to use AI
points.gist: Legitimate uses may include summarising and analysing materials, extracting findings, breaking writer's block and highlighting grammatical errors, especially in preparatory stages.

points.quote: If you are unclear or have queries about whether the use of any AI tools including generative AI may or may not be permitted for a particular assessment, please contact the Module Convenor in the first instance.
points.anchor: 3. AI and Academic Integrity and Misconduct
points.gist: Contact the Module Convenor first if unclear whether AI use is permitted for an assessment.
